reviews.title: Best Remote Desktop App, but Frustrating iPadOS Issues
reviews.text:
I genuinely love Jump Desktop. It’s easily the best remote desktop app I’ve ever used, which makes giving it one star even more frustrating.

On my 13-inch iPad Pro, the iPadOS status bar overlaps the macOS menu bar when connected to my Mac. This makes it difficult to see or interact with menu bar items, including Control Center on the mac. The only workaround I’ve found is enabling Guided Access, which isn’t ideal.

Another issue is Command + Q. Naturally, when using my Mac remotely, I press Cmd + Q to quit an application, but this quits Jump Desktop instead. It would be great to have an option to forward this shortcut to the remote Mac. Not a deal breaker, but definitely something worth improving.

To the developers: You genuinely don’t deserve a one star rating. You’ve built an incredible app, and I really appreciate your work! I’m only giving it one star to draw attention to these issues, particularly the status bar overlap. I’ll keep updating this review and will happily raise my rating once that issue is fixed.

Keep up the great work!

reviews.title: Problems, problems and no help

I did not receive that email. I even looked in spam. It was not there. I tried signing up again – multiple times in fact because there was no way for me to request that the email be resent. I tried to contact Jump – it was not easy. I’ve sent multiple emails and received no response. The only thing jump did right was Bill my account and send me an email receipt TO MY EMAIL. There is no such thing as help with this application. There is obviously no way to talk to a live person. And the only thing that worked was Jump got my money. There is a real problem with your app. It might be nice for you to fix it. In the meantime, can you refund my money?

reviews.title: Beware of huge battery drain running in background!
reviews.text: The app itself works very well to connect to my remote devices. Sadly however I just discovered what appears to be a major bug / issue with this app and wanted to potentially warn others. Used it Wednesday night to remote into my computer and then didn’t open it again. Thursday and Friday my phone’s battery was getting zapped (with little use). Finally checked my battery page Friday at 1PM, and discovered “Jump” had used up 31% of my battery since the morning! Also on Thursday it used 55% of my battery. All of this drain was with 0 on screen time and only from “running” in the background. I checked settings and there’s no option to disable background app refresh, so it appears the only current “fix” is to force close the app immediately when you’re finished using it. Quite disappointing to have to overthink using this app that it’ll zap your battery if you’re not aware of this issue.

Not worth $15, but now I know why they don’t offer a free trial, probably no one would buy it if they saw this limitation up front

reviews.title: Would Love to See AVP Fixes
reviews.text: I have been trying to find an ideal way to remote into my Windows PC. This has more flexibility that the Windows (rpd) app, but is also not optimized for the AVP unfortunately. The multi-screen option is DOA because it letterboxes all screens to the aspect ratio of an “iPad”, making them hard to see. I hoped I could launch multiple connections to the same computer, but it seems not, a second connection disconnects the first. My magictrackpad works nominally, but still can only do cursor + two finger scroll. Pinching zooms on the rdp client, not the host regardless of input mode. I cannot get any other multi-touch input gestures working. They work with the trackpad connected directly to the PC and I hoped this would pass that through better than alternatives. I will definitely re-visit this app if improvements are made for the AVP. Very close to what I need.
